guard_streams.write_limit: Corporate objectives, budgets, targets and programme descriptions are planning evidence, not current selected-parcel serviceability or measured speed.

facts.detail: BDUK's mission is fast and reliable digital connectivity for UK homes and businesses.
The 2024/25 plan is a companion to the multi-year 2023–2026 plan.
It focuses on objectives for the year ending 31 March 2025.
BDUK identifies Project Gigabit and the Shared Rural Network as its flagship programmes.
Project Gigabit is described as a £5 billion programme.
The programme supports nationwide gigabit-capable broadband by 2030.
The plan states Project Gigabit launched in March 2021.
Project Gigabit is delivered through four interventions.
The 2024/25 capital budget listed £461.8 million for Project Gigabit and £87.1 million for SRN.
Project Gigabit procurement assigns 10 percent of bid scoring to social value.

guard_streams.write_limit: Multi-year delivery trajectories and strategic targets do not prove current orderability or measured performance for selected parcels.

facts.detail: The plan's first objective is gigabit connectivity outside suppliers' commercial rollout plans.
Its second objective is improved mobile connectivity through SRN.
A third objective concerns making BDUK a strong workplace.
A fourth objective concerns financial management, governance and risk.
The plan proposed 1.56 million premises passed by BDUK interventions by the end of 2025.
The trajectory supported at least 85 percent total UK gigabit coverage by the end of 2025.
The plan cited a £5 billion lifetime budget and £1.2 billion to the end of 2024/25.
It estimated fewer than one percent of premises could remain outside Project Gigabit because of cost.
The plan commits to quarterly delivery updates and annual performance reporting.
It cited nearly £35 billion of announced commercial broadband investment.
